identity.title: Ultrasensitive endogenous miRNA imaging in live cells by an allosteric orthogonal CRISPR probe.

content.abstract: Sensitive and multiplexed visualization of endogenous RNA in living cells remains challenging because of insufficient signal amplification, background activation, and interference between parallel readout pathways, particularly for low-abundance regulatory RNAs. Many current CRISPR-based RNA imaging strategies rely on stoichiometric RNA binding, limiting sensitivity and often yielding a poor signal-to-background ratio for low-abundance endogenous microRNAs (miRNAs). Moreover, limited orthogonality between sensing modules and readouts complicates interference-free multiplexing. Inefficient intracellular delivery further limits their applicability in complex biological environments. Here, we introduce an allosteric CRISPR probe for orthogonal and amplified miRNA imaging in living cells, which is built on an allosterically gated crRNA that integrates a CRISPR-Cas12a system with a Zn(2+)-dependent DNAzyme module. Mechanistically, miR-210 selectively unlocks the caged crRNA to activate Cas12a trans-cleavage, providing amplified red (Cy5) fluorescence, while miR-21 independently activates DNAzyme cleavage to generate green (FAM) fluorescence with minimal cross-talk. Black phosphorus nanosheets serve as a biocompatible nanocarrier for efficient intracellular probe delivery. This orthogonal architecture enables precise discrimination of breast cancer subtypes in living cells and clinical tissue sections. Together, this work overcomes a central limitation of live-cell miRNA imaging by enabling sensitive and multiplexed visualization of endogenous miRNAs, opening new possibilities for dissecting RNA-mediated regulation in complex cellular systems.
